title: How Islamophobia Was Built Into U.S. Policy and Law Even Before 9/11
author: Team Zeteo
content:
Constant surveillance, [anti-immigration policies](https://zeteo.com/p/this-
week-in-democracy-week-84-trump), and [open
hatred](https://zeteo.com/p/the-7-most-islamophobic-things-that)… Has
Islamophobia in the U.S. gotten _worse_ since 9/11? And did anti-Muslim
bigotry in America exist long before then?

_Yes_ and _yes_ , argues journalist and author **Rozina Ali** , as she joins
**Mehdi** for a conversation about the history of Islamophobia and her
powerful new book, _Seasons of Fury: Four Families and the Rise of
Islamophobia in America_.

[Subscribe now](https://zeteo.com/subscribe)

Ali's book examines the way Islamophobia is **" manufactured and encouraged"
**in the U.S., tracing its roots back well before 9/11, to the 1940s. Today,
xenophobic persecution is not reserved for Muslims. Ali explains how the
Donald Trump administration is using vague anti-terror laws to target anyone
it deems a political enemy.

Watch the **full video** to hear Ali break down the way **" thousands and
thousands"** of Muslim Americans were surveilled by the FBI and undercover
informants, and explore the role Israel and Benjamin Netanyahu played in
shaping what we know to be Islamophobia today.
